content: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate interacts with various drugs and substances by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, as well as P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. These interactions can lead to significant changes in drug levels, effects, and potential toxicities. Below are the detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Fosamprenavir: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Fosaprepitant: Fosaprepitant increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Foscarnet: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and foscarnet increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 4. Fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin decreases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Fostamatinib: Fostamatinib increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Fostamatinib may also increase concentrations of P-gp substrates, requiring dosage adjustments. 6. Fostemsavir: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and fostemsavir increase the QTc interval. Fostemsavir also inhibits OATP1B1/3 transporters, which may necessitate dose modifications of coadministered OATP1B1/3 substrates. Avoid coadministration or modify therapy and monitor closely. 7. Gadobenate: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and gadobenate increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Gemifloxacin: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and gemifloxacin increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Gemtuzumab: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and gemtuzumab increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Gentamicin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of gentamicin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Gepirone: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of gepirone via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 12. Gilteritinib: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and gilteritinib increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Givinostat: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and givinostat increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline, during treatment, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if QTc >500 ms or if there is a >60 ms change from baseline. 14. Glasdegib: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and glasdegib increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation risk. 15. Goserelin: Goserelin increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Granisetron: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and granisetron increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Grapefruit: Grapefruit increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Griseofulvin: Griseofulvin decreases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Guanfacine: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of guanfacine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the guanfacine dose to half the recommended dose when coadministered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 20. Haloperidol: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and haloperidol increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Heparin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the effects of heparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Histrelin: Histrelin increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Hydrocortisone: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of hydrocortisone via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Hydrocortisone also decreases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and hydroxychloroquine sulfate increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Hydroxyprogesterone caproate: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of hydroxyprogesterone caproate via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Hydroxyzine: Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Ibrutinib: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of ibrutinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 28. Ibutinide: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ibutinide increase the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Idelalisib: Idelalisib increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Ifosfamide: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the level or effect of ifosfamide via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Iloperidone: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and iloperidone increase the QTc interval. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate also increases the level or effect of iloperidone via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Imatinib: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of imatinib via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Imipramine: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and imipramine increase the QTc interval. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate also increases the level or effect of imipramine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Indacaterol (inhaled): Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of indacaterol via modulation of P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 activities. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Indapamide: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and indapamide increase the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 36. Indinavir: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of indinavir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir also increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Infigratinib: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of infigratinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Inotuzumab: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and inotuzumab increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs and monitor electrolytes before and during treatment. 39. Irinotecan: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of irinotecan via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Isavuconazonium sulfate: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Isoflurane: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and isoflurane increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Isoniazid: Isoniazid increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Isradipine: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of isradipine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Istradefylline: Istradefylline increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. 45. Itraconazole: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and itraconazole increase the QTc interval. They also increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Ivabradine: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of ivabradine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Ivacaftor: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of ivacaftor via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ivacaftor dose when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 48. Ivermectin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of ivermectin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Ivosidenib: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of ivosidenib via CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of QTc prolongation. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 50. Ixabepilone: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of ixabepilone via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 51. Ketoconazole: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ketoconazole increase the QTc interval. They also increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 52. Lansoprazole: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the level or effect of lansoprazole via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 53. Lapatinib: Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and lapatinib increase the QTc interval. They also increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
